# BMad

You are BMad, master of the BMad Method. Speak in the first person as BMad, greet the user by name if it is known, be helpful and guiding and introduce yourself as the BMad Agent. You are the user's advisor across every BMad module they have installed: you know what each skill is for and how they fit together, you recommend the next step and say why, you talk through how to reach their goals with what they have, and you run skills for them when they ask. You also set up and maintain their installation. Be direct and opinionated. Answer in the configured communication language when you know it, otherwise in the user's language.

`{project-root}` is the nearest folder containing `_bmad/`, starting at the project working directory and moving up through its parents. `{skill-root}` is this skill's own folder.

## Actions

When the request is only one of these actions, load its reference and follow it.

- `references/setup.md`: setting up, updating, repairing or checking the installation, adding a module, or changing a config answer.
- `references/migrate.md`: migrating or converting this project's artifacts to a newer version of a module (`bmad migrate`), or what such a migration would change.
- `references/initiative.md`: which initiative is active, or switching, creating or clearing one, including when another skill hands off to set one.

## Help and conversation

Skip this section while the request is only a setup, migrate or initiative action; loading the help then only fills context. If the user later asks a question or wants advice, come back and follow it.

Everything else is help: a question, a discussion, what to do next, where to start, how to use the installed modules, or running a sequence of skills. Every help answer comes from the installed modules' own help, never from memory of BMad or inference from skill names. Before answering:

1. Run `uv run {skill-root}/scripts/knowledge.py --content` with `--root <folder>` for each skills folder the host has active, project folders first. It returns the full help of every installed module and lists the topic files each one offers.
2. Read `references/help.md` and follow it.

Core Tools knowledge

This document covers the skills of the `core-tools` module: what each one is for and when to recommend it.

## How the core tools fit

The core tools belong to no phase and no path. Each stands alone and works with or without any other module. Suggest one whenever it would help: before, during, after, or entirely outside another module's flow. Never present one as a required step. A project may hold only some of these skills: recommend from what is installed.

## Initiatives

An initiative is one body of work of any kind: a product, a feature, a book, a set of art assets. Its folder under `output_folder` holds what every module's skills write for that work. `active_initiative` under `[core]` in `_bmad/custom/config.user.toml` names the folder in use; the file is personal, so each person can work on a different one. With none active, work is written loose to `{output_folder}/`, and some skills first ask whether it belongs to an initiative. The `bmad` skill shows, switches, creates, or clears the active initiative. What goes inside the folder is up to each module: its help says.

## Start here

- No idea yet, or wants more and better ideas on a topic → `bmad-brainstorming`.
- Has an idea and is not sure it holds up → `bmad-forge-idea`.
- Needs facts from outside before deciding (a market, a technology, competitors, what users say), has a research report to make usable, or wants their own code researched (how something works, why it is built that way, the code a ticket depends on) → `bmad-deep-recon`.
- Needs to write a document: a decision record or ADR, a postmortem, a proposal or grant application, a security review or threat model, a pitch deck or talk, or any document from the team's own template → `bmad-facilitate`. A PRD goes to John (`bmad-agent-pm`); a product brief, PRFAQ or BRD to Mary (`bmad-agent-analyst`).
- Has a piece of work and wants it better:
  - They have a draft in front of them (theirs or the model's) and want it pushed further, or want a critique method run on it → `bmad-advanced-elicitation`. It starts only by name: tell them to say "advanced elicitation", with the method if they have one in mind.
  - They ask for a review of a diff, a file, or a document → `bmad-review`.
  - They want several points of view arguing it out, a roundtable, or a focus group of their customers → `bmad-party-mode`.
- Has large or raw input:
  - A transcript, a chat or email thread, a voice memo, or a long document they want what matters from (decisions, action items, key points) → `bmad-ingest`.
  - A document past about 50 KB that agents work from (an old spec, a vendor manual, a large PRD), or one already sharded that they want to change → `bmad-shard-pro`. A long document that is kept and edited is split; one that has to stay one file, or a fixed reference, gets a contents list (`help/shard-pro.md`). A document under about 50 KB needs nothing, including one a planning skill just wrote.
  - About to start a PRD, brief, architecture or tickets with large inputs: suggest preparing them first, raw inputs through `bmad-ingest` and documents past about 50 KB through `bmad-shard-pro`, so the planning skill reads short notes and only the parts it needs.
  - A sharded document is the input to another skill: give that skill the folder's main file, named after the folder, which links to every shard.
- BMad itself needs attention:
  - Something was installed or updated, or a skill reports that BMad is not set up or a BMad script was not found → `bmad setup`.
  - "What do I have, and is it current?" → `bmad status`.
  - Which initiative is active, or they want to switch, create, or clear one → `bmad`.
  - They want a skill, an agent or a document it writes to behave differently, such as a section the PRD must have, HTML by default, or the team's own template → `bmad-customize`. They need not know which skill writes the document.
  - They ask what a BMad module is or how to make one → `help/modules.md`.

## The skills

| Skill | For | Good to know | Writes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bmad-brainstorming` | A coached session that pushes well past the obvious ideas. | The user picks who supplies the ideas: themselves, both, or the skill alone. It does not judge ideas until asked to converge. Sessions resume. | `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/brainstorm-<topic>/`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work, with `brainstorm.html` and, on request, `brainstorm-<topic>.md`: the chosen ideas, ready as input to any installed planning skill. |
| `bmad-forge-idea` | Questions one half-formed idea hard until the user can act on it or drop it. | Any idea, not only products, including a change to an existing project. It ends hardened, killed, or clearer, and all three are good outcomes. Not for generating ideas or for outside facts. | `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/forge-<slug>/`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work, with `forge-report.html` and, when the idea hardens, `forge-<slug>.md`: the surviving decisions, ready as input to any installed planning or build skill. |
| `bmad-deep-recon` | Research that serves a decision, with cited sources found now, never from memory. | It can draft a prompt for the user's own research tool, process a finished report, or run the research here. It can also choose between candidates, or answer questions about this repository from its code and git history. | `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/research-<topic>/`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work, with `brief.md` and `research-<topic>.md`, which is input for whatever skill acts on the decision. Codebase research also writes each ADR the user approves, beside the code it governs. |
| `bmad-facilitate` | Coaches the user through one document from a template library, then updates or validates it later. | Its templates come from installed modules: Method's `decision-record`, `postmortem` and `security-review`, Founder's `proposal` and `pitch-deck`, and the Creative Intelligence Suite's `character`, from CIS 0.4.0. A team adds or replaces templates and adds rules to shipped ones. Rigor follows the stakes the user states. Unfinished runs resume. With no fitting template it builds a structure and offers to save it. | `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/<id>-<slug>/`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work, with `<id>-<slug>.md`, `.memlog.md`, review files and, when rendered, `<id>-<slug>.html`. |
| `bmad-advanced-elicitation` | Pushes a draft off its first answer and proposes a revision. | It names the draft and where it is weak and starts right away: a best-fit critique method and a wildcard (pre-mortem, steelman, first principles, red team, and more) as independent readers, plus an open push for a single choice or a second method for a document, then one proposed revision with each push's findings. Nothing changes unless the user accepts. It starts only when named, and a method named when invoking it runs straight away. | `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/elicitation-<topic>/`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work, with each push's findings and a report of every round. The work itself changes only where the user accepts. |
| `bmad-review` | Independent review lenses over any diff or document: adversarial, edge cases, verification gaps, structure, prose. | It runs only when the user asks and says "review". Acting on earlier findings is a change, not a review. No severity ranking. | The report in chat, or a file when the project sets a report path. |
| `bmad-party-mode` | A group conversation between agents or personas, with the user in the room. | It works alone or beside any skill. Custom parties, a default party, and memory are all configurable, and a module can ship a cast. It debates and does not verify. | On request, a keepsake `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/party-<slug>/party-<slug>.html`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work. Memory under `{output_folder}/party-mode/memories/`. |
| `bmad-shard-pro` | Makes a long markdown or text document cheap for an agent to navigate: leaves it, adds a contents list, or splits it word for word into shards. | It may recommend not splitting, and never rewrites content. Any agent can change it later by following the note in its main file. | In the document's own folder: a main file named after the folder that links to every shard, the shards, and the frozen original in `.source/`. |
| `bmad-ingest` | Turns raw input into a cited note an agent or person acts on instead of the raw: decisions, action items, open questions, key points. | The note's shape comes from a template; teams and modules add their own. Every item points back to the raw, and a review pass checks it. Other skills can call it on their inputs. | The original, unchanged, in `{output_folder}/raw/`; the note in the calling skill's folder, such as a PRD's `sources/`, else `{output_folder}/notes/`. |
| `bmad-customize` | Changes how an installed skill or agent behaves without editing it: persona, standing facts, templates, output paths, steps on completion, and what a document such as the PRD asks for, contains or renders. | Team overrides are committed and shared; personal ones are not. It offers only what the target skill exposes. A document change extends its template, so updates to the original still arrive. Central config is edited by hand. | `{project-root}/_bmad/custom/{skill-name}.toml` for the team, `{skill-name}.user.toml` for one person; a document change in `{project-root}/_bmad/custom/facilitate-templates/`. |

## `bmad`: setup, status, and help

- `bmad setup` creates and repairs `{project-root}/_bmad`, including the shared scripts other skills call, and asks each installed module's new configuration questions. Recommend it after anything is installed or updated.
- `bmad status` changes nothing. It reports what is installed, what is missing or out of date, and the one command to run next.
- Either takes a module code, such as `bmad setup core-tools`, to cover that module only.
- To add a module that is not installed, such as the Test Architect, run `npx skills add bmad-code-org/bmad-method-test-architecture-enterprise`, then `bmad setup tea`.
- BMad is installed per project. To use it in another repository, run `npx skills add bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD` there, then `bmad setup`.

## More detail

This document should be enough to route the user and say what to do next. Each topic file below sits in this folder and goes deeper on one subject. Read one only when the question is about that subject, using the path the knowledge script lists for it. For how one skill behaves in detail, that skill's own files are the last resort.

| Topic file | Read when the user asks about |
|---|---|
| `help/advanced-elicitation.md` | How to start and aim `bmad-advanced-elicitation`, what it runs when no methods are named, what comes back, default and custom methods, when a plain "push harder" is enough. |
| `help/party-mode.md` | What party mode is good for alone or with other skills, custom parties, the default party, memory, parties that come with a module. |
| `help/research.md` | Getting the most from `bmad-deep-recon` and which of its services to use. |
| `help/facilitate.md` | What `bmad-facilitate` can write and how to list every template available here, so open it before saying what the user can be coached through. Also its shipped templates, calling it directly, a team's own templates and extensions. |
| `help/customization.md` | How overrides work: team or personal file, how they merge, central config, an override that is not applied, resetting. |
| `help/team-adoption.md` | Making a whole team's BMad follow shared rules, tools, templates, and publishing steps. |
| `help/ingest.md` | Processing transcripts, threads, recordings or long reports, ingest's templates and adding them, where the original and the note go, ingest inside a PRD or other work, sensitive recordings. |
| `help/shard-pro.md` | Whether to shard a document, contents list or split, how a sharded document works, `.source/`, changing one, handing one to another skill. |
| `help/modules.md` | What a BMad module is, each file in one, a single-skill module, a module that only ships personas and parties, building one. |

## When this document is not enough

For a `core-tools` question this document, its topic files, and the installed skills cannot answer, fetch the documentation site at `https://docs.bmad-method.org/` and follow the pages relevant to the question. The source repository it links to is the final authority on how anything actually behaves.

This document covers the skills of the `method` module: what each one gives the user, when to recommend it, and what to offer next.

## How the method works

The method turns an intent of any size into working software. Recommend the smallest path that safely fits the work; never march the user through every skill. A project may hold only some of these skills: recommend from what is installed, and say plainly when a step has no installed skill rather than inventing a substitute.

**The ticket is the spec.** The initiative, epic or story file is the spec at its level. Every skill that works on a ticket reads it first and in full and trusts it; its `sources:` are re-read only by Sofia when she updates it, and a `companions:` file only where the ticket points. Talk to Sofia the Product Owner (`bmad-agent-po`) to fill its Requirements from whatever the user has (a PRD, a brief, notes, a transcript), keep it in step with its sources, and slice from it.

A transcript, a chat or email thread, or a voice memo goes through `bmad-ingest` first when it is installed, and the note it returns is the input. A sharded document is given to any skill as its main file, named after its folder, which links to every shard. The method adds note templates for `standup`, `retrospective` (the meeting, not `bmad-retrospective`'s epic review), `sprint-review`, `discovery-workshop` and `user-interview`.

The four phases are analysis (ideation, research, is it worth building), planning (what exactly, and in what slices), implementation (build it), and validation (is it right). They describe what kind of help a skill gives. They are not a mandatory sequence to complete.

Project size decides how many build sessions the work needs. Stakes decide how heavy the planning gets. A large hobby project keeps planning light; a small change to a regulated system may not.

## More detail

This document should be enough to route the user and say what to do next. Each topic file below sits in this folder and goes deeper on one subject. Read one only when the question is about that subject, using the path the knowledge script lists for it.

| Topic file | Read when the user asks about |
|---|---|
| `help/analysis-skills.md` | The brief or the PRFAQ from Mary (`bmad-agent-analyst`) in depth: what each gives, when to pick it, when not to, how they relate. |
| `help/planning-skills.md` | `bmad-agent-po` (Sofia), `bmad-agent-pm` (John) and his planning documents, `bmad-ux`, `bmad-architecture` in depth, and customizing John's templates. |
| `help/implementation-skills.md` | `bmad-build` or `bmad-build-auto` in depth. |
| `help/validation-skills.md` | `bmad-code-review`, `bmad-walkthrough`, `bmad-qa-generate-e2e-tests`, or `bmad-retrospective` in depth. |
| `help/prototyping.md` | Prototyping or vibe coding first, what a prototype is good for (worth doing, feasibility, complexity, unknowns), non-engineers prototyping, what to do with a prototype afterwards, whether planning still matters after a good first version. |
| `help/existing-codebase.md` | Using BMad on an inherited, brownfield, or long-lived codebase. |
| `help/preparing-a-repo-for-agents.md` | Getting a codebase ready for agentic coding, inconsistent agent output, how much documentation to keep (small ADRs, not heavy docs), regular refactoring, holding quality over time. |
| `help/artifact-lifetime.md` | Whether to keep PRDs, specs, stories, and build records after the work is done, archiving, closing out an epic, keeping old plans from misleading agents. |
| `help/monorepo-and-polyrepo.md` | Where to install BMad and keep planning when work spans one repository or several; the workspace layout for a poly repo. |
| `help/working-in-an-organization.md` | A team or enterprise: an existing PRD, Jira or another tracker, approvals and sign-off, document owners, several engineers in parallel, requirements changing mid-flight. |
| `help/ticketing-and-epics.md` | How Sofia's ticket tree works (initiatives, planning an epic's stories, the breakdown, building from an entry, refining), plan status, review, and retrospective. |
| `help/ticketing-setup.md` | Setting up and driving the ticket tree with Sofia: the store, several repos, trackers, the phrases to say, the hand-off to `bmad-build`. |

    F -->|open questions or assumptions| F1["Talk to Sofia the Product Owner to resolve them<br/>answers go to the source, the ticket, or both"]

    S2 --> G{"Would separately built epics have to share decisions?<br/>stack, contracts, formats, hosting"}
    G -->|yes| G1["bmad-architecture reads the initiative<br/>then talk to Sofia the Product Owner to adopt it as a companion the epics cite"]
    G -->|no| H
    G1 --> H
    F1 & F2 --> F
    F -->|sliced, epics remain| H

    H{"State of each epic file"} -->|refined: false| S7["Talk to Sofia the Product Owner to refine the epic, scaled to the initiative<br/>each open point settled now, spiked, or left to the stories; the user may add a PRD from John, or a bmad-ux, bmad-architecture or bmad-deep-recon run on the epic"]
    H -->|refined, no entries| S3["Talk to Sofia the Product Owner to plan the epic's stories: entries in tickets.toml"]
    H -->|an entry needs criteria first: a bug, refine = true| S5["Talk to Sofia the Product Owner to refine it"]
    H -->|entries ready| I["bmad-build per entry<br/>bmad-build-auto when no one is present"]
    H -->|blocked| S6["Talk to Sofia the Product Owner to settle it as a dated Decision, or spike it"]
    H -->|a change surfaced mid-build| S4["Talk to Sofia the Product Owner to replan: she updates, re-slices or drops, and records the Decision"]

Rules the diagram leans on:

Sofia the Product Owner takes more than one input.
- A prototype fits anywhere before the initiative file, and suits enterprise work, hobby work, and non-engineers; a throwaway needs no skill. Thrown away, talk to Sofia the Product Owner to write the initiative from its notes; kept, it is an existing codebase (`help/prototyping.md`).
- Risk, unclear requirements, architectural reach, or several people push work up from one session even when it is small.
- An epic file with no `refined` key counts as refined.
- Mid-path, recommend the next unfinished step of the route the user is on, not a restart. After a change, work resumes at the earliest affected step; unaffected work is not replayed.

They describe what kind of help a skill gives. They are not a mandatory sequence to complete. 127 128 Project size decides how many build sessions the work needs. Stakes decide how heavy the planning gets. A large hobby project keeps planning light; a small change to a regulated system may not. 129 130 ## More detail 131 132 This document should be enough to route the user and say what to do next. Each topic file below sits in this folder and goes deeper on one subject. Read one only when the question is about that subject, using the path the knowledge script lists for it. 133 134 | Topic file | Read when the user asks about | 135 |---|---| 136 | `help/analysis-skills.md` | The brief or the PRFAQ from Mary (`bmad-agent-analyst`) in depth: what each gives, when to pick it, when not to, how they relate. | 137 | `help/planning-skills.md` | `bmad-agent-po` (Sofia), `bmad-agent-pm` (John) and his planning documents, `bmad-ux`, `bmad-architecture` in depth, and customizing John's templates. | 138 | `help/implementation-skills.md` | `bmad-build` or `bmad-build-auto` in depth. | 139 | `help/validation-skills.md` | `bmad-code-review`, `bmad-walkthrough`, `bmad-qa-generate-e2e-tests`, or `bmad-retrospective` in depth. | 140 | `help/prototyping.md` | Prototyping or vibe coding first, what a prototype is good for (worth doing, feasibility, complexity, unknowns), non-engineers prototyping, what to do with a prototype afterwards, whether planning still matters after a good first version. | 141 | `help/existing-codebase.md` | Using BMad on an inherited, brownfield, or long-lived codebase. | 142 | `help/preparing-a-repo-for-agents.md` | Getting a codebase ready for agentic coding, inconsistent agent output, how much documentation to keep (small ADRs, not heavy docs), regular refactoring, holding quality over time. | 143 | `help/artifact-lifetime.md` | Whether to keep PRDs, specs, stories, and build records after the work is done, archiving, closing out an epic, keeping old plans from misleading agents. | 144 | `help/monorepo-and-polyrepo.md` | Where to install BMad and keep planning when work spans one repository or several; the workspace layout for a poly repo. | 145 | `help/working-in-an-organization.md` | A team or enterprise: an existing PRD, Jira or another tracker, approvals and sign-off, document owners, several engineers in parallel, requirements changing mid-flight. | 146 | `help/ticketing-and-epics.md` | How Sofia's ticket tree works (initiatives, planning an epic's stories, the breakdown, building from an entry, refining), plan status, review, and retrospective. | 147 | `help/ticketing-setup.md` | Setting up and driving the ticket tree with Sofia: the store, several repos, trackers, the phrases to say, the hand-off to `bmad-build`. | 148 | `help/unattended-builds.md` | `bmad-build-auto`, building stories with no human present, a blocked run and how to retry, what to check after a run. | 149 | `help/review-choices.md` | Review depth, skipping review, another review pass, when to stop, slow reviews, customizing review. | 150 | `help/project-context.md` | `bmad-project-context` in depth: what belongs in `AGENTS.md`, why the block is small, its intents, removing a rule. | 151 152 ## Routing 153 154 Every "what next" is answered by the state of the spec at its altitude: the initiative file, then each epic file. Upstream skills exist to feed it. 155 156 ```mermaid 157 flowchart TD 158 A(["Request"]) --> B{"One session can understand, build, review and finish it?"} 159 B -->|obvious, low-risk edit| B1(["Just edit. No skill"]) 160 B -->|yes| B2(["bmad-build"]) 161 B -->|no| C{"Initiative file exists?
an active initiative may be set with none written yet"} 162 163 C -->|no| D{"Work the idea out before it becomes the spec?
the user wants to, or cannot yet say what it is"} 164 D -->|no| S1["Talk to Sofia the Product Owner to write the initiative from what exists: a PRD, UX, a brief, notes, an idea explained

Sofia the Product Owner takes more than one input. 201 - A prototype fits anywhere before the initiative file, and suits enterprise work, hobby work, and non-engineers; a throwaway needs no skill. Thrown away, talk to Sofia the Product Owner to write the initiative from its notes; kept, it is an existing codebase (`help/prototyping.md`). 202 - Risk, unclear requirements, architectural reach, or several people push work up from one session even when it is small. 203 - An epic file with no `refined` key counts as refined. 204 - Mid-path, recommend the next unfinished step of the route the user is on, not a restart. After a change, work resumes at the earliest affected step; unaffected work is not replayed. 205 - After `bmad-build`: open a PR, or `bmad-qa-generate-e2e-tests` when end-to-end coverage is wanted. The work is complete when the intent is satisfied, its chosen checks pass, and no chosen review leaves material findings open, not when every skill has run. 206 207 ## Match the situation 208 209 Situations the diagram does not settle. 210 211 | The user says or has | Recommend | Because | 212 |---|---|---| 213 | "Create a spec", "write the initiative", "distill this PRD", "slice this", "tickets", "what's ready", "where are we", "this changed, what now", "ask Sofia", "the product owner" | Talk to Sofia the Product Owner (`bmad-agent-po`) to do what the phrase says | Each phrase dispatches to one of her capabilities (SPEC, TICKETS, REFINE, BOARD, VALIDATE, REPLAN, STORE); no menu is shown. | 214 | "Create a PRD", "write the PRD", "update the PRD", "validate this PRD", "review my PRD", "write the business case", "draft the program charter", "shape a pitch", "plan the launch", "ask John", "the PM", "the product manager" | Talk to John the Product Manager (`bmad-agent-pm`) to do what the phrase says | Each phrase dispatches to one of his capabilities (CREATE, UPDATE, VALIDATE); he picks the document from the altitude. | 215 | "Write a product brief", "create a PRFAQ", "work backwards", "run the PRFAQ challenge", "stress-test this concept", "write the BRD", "market research", "competitive analysis", "ask Mary", "the analyst" | Talk to Mary the Business Analyst (`bmad-agent-analyst`) to do what the phrase says | Each phrase dispatches to one of her capabilities (BRAINSTORM, RESEARCH, CREATE, UPDATE, VALIDATE, CONTEXT); she picks the document from what the user wants. | 216 | One bug or story to track, with no epic to hold it | Talk to Sofia the Product Owner to write it as a `backlog/` ticket, or an entry in the epic the user names | Standalone leaves live in `backlog/`, are refined first, and build like any entry. | 217 | The work is more than one initiative's worth | Talk to Sofia the Product Owner to propose a parent initiative | The parent is an ordinary initiative whose breakdown lists child initiatives in build order; each child keeps initiative, epic and story. Set the active initiative to the child being worked, or to the parent to see the whole. | 218 | Work spans several repositories | Install BMad at a workspace root that holds them all, with planning kept there | One session then reaches the plan and every project (`help/monorepo-and-polyrepo.md`). | 219 | "How do I get my repo ready for AI agents?", or agents keep producing inconsistent work | Consistent patterns, a good initial `AGENTS.md`, end-to-end tests, and cleanup first when quality is low | Agents copy what they find (`help/preparing-a-repo-for-agents.md`). | 220 | An inherited or brownfield codebase | A small `bmad-build` change first; `bmad-project-context` and `bmad-walkthrough` as needed | No up-front documentation pass is required (`help/existing-codebase.md`). | 221 | A team with an existing PRD, a tracker, approvals, or several engineers | The full path only when approvers, parallel teams, or required documents call for it | The existing PRD is input, each document has one owner, and sign-off attaches to skill results (`help/working-in-an-organization.md`). | 222 | Wants tickets or a tracker (Jira, Linear, GitHub) as the record | Talk to Sofia the Product Owner to connect it | Tickets are the board. | 223 | A v6 project (`epics.md`, `sprint-status.yaml`, dated folders under the planning folder) that wants the v7 layout | `bmad migrate method`, before anything else | The module ships `migration-1.toml`: the rules for turning the planning folder into an initiative, moving document folders into it whole, and turning epics and sprint status into a ticket tree. Unrecognized files outside the planning folder stay where they are. The `bmad` skill plans it with the user, then performs it. | 224 | `tickets.py` stops with an error naming `bmad migrate`, or `tickets.toml` or epic folders sit directly in an initiative folder | `bmad migrate method` | The module ships `migration-2.toml`: it moves each initiative's and epic's breakdown into a `tickets/` folder inside it and rewrites the paths that pointed at the moved files. | 225 226 ## The skills 227 228 One line per skill: what it is for and what it writes. Paths are in the active initiative's folder, `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/`, or in `{output_folder}/` when none is active; each document is a `-/` folder holding `-.md`. A document from John, or a `bmad-ux` or `bmad-architecture` run, on an epic lands in the epic's folder instead, and Sofia adopts it as the epic's companion. Each initiative's and epic's breakdown sits in a `tickets/` folder inside it. With no active initiative, `bmad-agent-po` offers to create one; the other planning skills hand off to the `bmad` skill to set one. Showing, switching, creating, or clearing the active initiative is a `bmad` request. `planning_artifacts` and `implementation_artifacts` are no longer read. 229 230 | Skill | For | Writes | 231 |---|---|---| 232 | **Analysis** (`help/analysis-skills.md`) | | | 233 | `bmad-agent-analyst` | Mary the Business Analyst brainstorms and researches with the user, then coaches a brief (a 1-2 page account of a product the user believes in; it does not judge the idea), a PRFAQ (tests whether a concept survives scrutiny: press release, hard FAQs, researched claims, a verdict) or a business requirements document out of them. | `brief-/brief-.md`, `prfaq-/prfaq-.md`, `brd-/brd-.md` | 234 | **Planning** (`help/planning-skills.md`) | | | 235 | `bmad-agent-po` | Sofia the Product Owner. Writes a ticket's Requirements and Constraints from any input, with a stable `R` id per line naming its source, naming the gaps and walking them with the user, or recording each as an Open question line, when the input is sparse, and updates them when the input changes. Slices initiatives into thin epics and epics into stories, refines an epic or a story, runs the board (start, block, close, drop), validates, replans a change mid-flight, and connects a tracker. Stories are entries in `tickets.toml`; a file is written only when one is reviewed, refined, or published. A bug is a `backlog/` file or an entry in its epic. | The ticket file, with `.memlog.md` and companions beside it; the ticket tree under `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/`, plus `{output_folder}/backlog/` | 236 | `bmad-agent-pm` | John the Product Manager coaches a planning document out of the user, picked by altitude and sized to the stakes: a PRD, light PRD, prototype plan, experiment card, spec for a coding agent, opportunity assessment, business case, program charter, strategy narrative, Shape Up pitch, requirements specification or launch plan. He also updates and validates them. | `-/-.md`, such as `prd-/prd-.md` | 237 | `bmad-ux` | How the product looks and works. May lead, follow, or stand alone. Can produce mocks and wireframes. | `ux-/` with `DESIGN.md`, `EXPERIENCE.md`, and `ux-.md` naming them | 238 | `bmad-architecture` | Settles only the decisions that keep separately built parts consistent. Coaches a user with no architecture knowledge, recommends a current starter, and covers hosting and deployment. | `architecture-/architecture-.md` | 239 | **Implementation** (`help/implementation-skills.md`) | | | 240 | `bmad-build` | One session of delivery: clarifies intent, plans, implements, reviews, commits. The default for any real change. Takes free text, a ticket from the tree (nothing means the next ready one), or any file as intent. Reads a ticket in full with its epic. | A ticket's plan beside `tickets.toml`, or `plan-.md`; `deferred-work.md` | 241 | `bmad-build-auto` | One unattended build of one ticket, dispatched by a loop or script. Never for attended work. | The same plans as `bmad-build` | 242 | **Validation** (`help/validation-skills.md`) | | | 243 | `bmad-code-review` | Agent review of any diff, PR, or branch, with triaged findings; with no argument it offers the tickets in review. Redundant right after a thorough `bmad-build` review of the same change. | A dated block in the plan's `## Code Review` section, or chat | 244 | `bmad-walkthrough` | The human reviews a change block by block, guided. Also a way to learn unfamiliar code. | `walkthrough-/` with the narrative and a `-log.md` | 245 | `bmad-qa-generate-e2e-tests` | API and end-to-end tests for features that already exist. | Tests where the project keeps its end-to-end tests; the report is in chat | 246 | `bmad-retrospective` | Judges a finished epic folder in the ticket tree as a whole against its Done when. | `epic--retrospective.md` in the epic folder, plus each approved `adr-.md` beside the code it governs, or in the decisions folder when system-wide | 247 | **Any time** (`help/project-context.md`) | | | 248 | `bmad-project-context` | Keeps a small, verified block of rules for agents. Use it when an agent got something wrong in this repo, a repo has no usable `AGENTS.md`, or the stack was just decided. It gives no repo overview. | `{project-root}/AGENTS.md` | 249 250 ### Who reviews what 251 252 | | Reviewer | Looks at | Fixes | 253 |---|---|---|---| 254 | Review inside `bmad-build` | Agents | The change just built | Clear findings, itself | 255 | `bmad-code-review` | Agents | Any diff, PR, branch, or commit | What the human chooses | 256 | `bmad-walkthrough` | The human, guided | A commit, PR, file, or directory | Nothing unless asked | 257 | `bmad-retrospective` | Agents, across tickets | A whole epic folder | Nothing; proposes action items | 258 259 ## The agents 260 261 Six named experts, each owning a phase and staying in the conversation across turns. An agent carries its role's judgment, offers a menu of the skills it owns, and helps the user decide what to do and why before and between skill runs. Offer one whenever the user wants an expert to work with rather than a single skill to run, is unsure where to begin in a phase, or likes the experience of interacting with unique personas. In the future these agents will have the ability to retain memory and work autonomously which is why they are still a core part of the project. 262 263 | Agent | Phase | Work with them to | 264 |---|---|---| 265 | Mary, analyst — `bmad-agent-analyst` | Analysis | Brainstorm, research a market, domain, technology, or competitor, then shape a brief or a PRFAQ, or write a business requirements document. | 266 | John, product manager — `bmad-agent-pm` | Planning | Turn a vision into a PRD or another planning document, and check readiness. | 267 | Sofia, product owner — `bmad-agent-po` | Planning | Write a ticket's requirements from whatever exists, slice it into epics and stories, run the board, and replan a change mid-flight. No menu: say what you want. | 268 | Sally, UX designer — `bmad-agent-ux-designer` | Planning | Work out how the product looks and behaves. | 269 | Winston, architect — `bmad-agent-architect` | Planning | Settle the technical decisions that keep the parts consistent, and check readiness. | 270 | Amelia, developer — `bmad-agent-dev` | Implementation and validation | Build stories, generate tests, review code, and run a retrospective. | 271 272 An agent and its skills are two ways into the same work: a skill run directly does the job, and an agent adds a guide who knows the whole phase. `bmad-party-mode` brings the agents together in one discussion and offers the `product-team` room. 273 274 ## When this document is not enough 275 276 For a `method` question this document, its topic files, and the installed skills cannot answer, fetch the documentation site at `https://docs.bmad-method.org/` and follow the pages relevant to the question. The source repository it links to is the final authority on how anything actually behaves. 277 278 # g2-hobby 279 _bmad-output: 280 initiative-meeting-room-booker 281 raw 282 283 _bmad-output/initiative-meeting-room-booker: 284 initiative-meeting-room-booker.md 285 tickets 286 287 _bmad-output/initiative-meeting-room-booker/tickets: 288 tickets.toml 289 290 _bmad-output/raw: 291 idea-meeting-room-booker.md 292 { 293 "core.output_folder": "{project-root}/_bmad-output", 294 "core.active_initiative": "initiative-meeting-room-booker" 295 } 296

roots [ ".claude/skills" ] documents topics [ { "module": "core-tools", "topic": "advanced-elicitation", "path": "help/advanced-elicitation.md", "file": ".claude/skills/bmod-core-tools/help/advanced-elicitation.md" }, { "module": " templates [ { "module": "method", "id": "agent-spec", "version": "1.1.0", "description": "One feature handed to a coding agent, with tests and acceptance.", "agents": [ "bmad-agent-pm" ] }, { migrations [ { "module": "method", "path": "migration-1.toml", "file": ".claude/skills/bmod-method/migration-1.toml", "from": "6", "to": "7", "title": "Move v6 planning and implementation artifacts problems [] ===== core-tools # BMad Core Tools knowledge This document covers the skills of the `core-tools` module: what each one is for and when to recommend it. ## How the core tools fit The core tools belong to no phase and no path. Each stands alone and works with or without any other module. Suggest one whenever it would help: before, during, after, or entirely outside another module's flow. Never present one as a required step. A project may hold only some of these skills: recommend from what is installed. ## Initiatives An initiative is one body of work of any kind: a product, a feature, a book, a set of art assets. Its folder under `output_folder` holds what every module's skills write for that work. `active_initiative` under `[core]` in `_bmad/custom/config.user.toml` names the folder in use; the file is personal, so each person can work on a different one. With none active, work is written loose to `{output_folder}/`, and some skills first ask whether it belongs to an initiative. The `bmad` skill shows, switches, creates, or clears the active initiative. What goes inside the folder is up to each module: its help says. ## Start here - No idea yet, or wants more and better ideas on a topic → `bmad-brainstorming`. - Has an idea and is not sure it holds up → `bmad-forge-idea`. - Needs facts from outside before deciding (a market, a technology, competitors, what users say), has a research report to make usable, or wants their own code researched (how something works, why it is built that way, the code a ticket depends on) → `bmad-deep-recon`. - Needs to write a document: a decision record or ADR, a postmortem, a proposal or grant application, a security review or threat model, a pitch deck or talk, or any document from the team's own template → `bmad-facilitate`. A PRD goes to John (`bmad-agent-pm`); a product brief, PRFAQ or BRD to Mary (`bmad-agent-analyst`). - Has a piece of work and wants it better: - They have a draft in front of them (theirs or the model's) and want it pushed further, or want a critique method run on it → `bmad-advanced-elicitation`. It starts only by name: tell them to say "advanced elicitation", with the method if they have one in mind. - They ask for a review of a diff, a file, or a document → `bmad-review`. - They want several points of view arguing it out, a roundtable, or a focus group of their customers → `bmad-party-mode`. - Has large or raw input: - A transcript, a chat or email thread, a voice memo, or a long document they want what matters from (decisions, action items, key points) → `bmad-ingest`. - A document past about 50 KB that agents work from (an old spec, a vendor manual, a large PRD), or one already sharded that they want to change → `bmad-shard-pro`. A long document that is kept and edited is split; one that has to stay one file, or a fixed reference, gets a contents list (`help/shard-pro.md`). A document under about 50 KB needs nothing, including one a planning skill just wrote. - About to start a PRD, brief, architecture or tickets with large inputs: suggest preparing them first, raw inputs through `bmad-ingest` and documents past about 50 KB through `bmad-shard-pro`, so the planning skill reads short notes and only the parts it needs. - A sharded document is the input to another skill: give that skill the folder's main file, named after the folder, which links to every shard. - BMad itself needs attention: - Something was installed or updated, or a skill reports that BMad is not set up or a BMad script was not found → `bmad setup`. - "What do I have, and is it current?" → `bmad status`. - Which initiative is active, or they want to switch, create, or clear one → `bmad`. - They want a skill, an agent or a document it writes to behave differently, such as a section the PRD must have, HTML by default, or the team's own template → `bmad-customize`. They need not know which skill writes the document. - They ask what a BMad module is or how to make one → `help/modules.md`. ## The skills | Skill | For | Good to know | Writes | |---|---|---|---| | `bmad-brainstorming` | A coached session that pushes well past the obvious ideas. | The user picks who supplies the ideas: themselves, both, or the skill alone. It does not judge ideas until asked to converge. Sessions resume. | `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/brainstorm-/`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work, with `brainstorm.html` and, on request, `brainstorm-.md`: the chosen ideas, ready as input to any installed planning skill. | | `bmad-forge-idea` | Questions one half-formed idea hard until the user can act on it or drop it. | Any idea, not only products, including a change to an existing project. It ends hardened, killed, or clearer, and all three are good outcomes. Not for generating ideas or for outside facts. | `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/forge-/`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work, with `forge-report.html` and, when the idea hardens, `forge-.md`: the surviving decisions, ready as input to any installed planning or build skill. | | `bmad-deep-recon` | Research that serves a decision, with cited sources found now, never from memory. | It can draft a prompt for the user's own research tool, process a finished report, or run the research here. It can also choose between candidates, or answer questions about this repository from its code and git history. | `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/research-/`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work, with `brief.md` and `research-.md`, which is input for whatever skill acts on the decision. Codebase research also writes each ADR the user approves, beside the code it governs. | | `bmad-facilitate` | Coaches the user through one document from a template library, then updates or validates it later. | Its templates come from installed modules: Method's `decision-record`, `postmortem` and `security-review`, Founder's `proposal` and `pitch-deck`, and the Creative Intelligence Suite's `character`, from CIS 0.4.0. A team adds or replaces templates and adds rules to shipped ones. Rigor follows the stakes the user states. Unfinished runs resume. With no fitting template it builds a structure and offers to save it. | `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/-/`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work, with `-.md`, `.memlog.md`, review files and, when rendered, `-.html`. | | `bmad-advanced-elicitation` | Pushes a draft off its first answer and proposes a revision. | It names the draft and where it is weak and starts right away: a best-fit critique method and a wildcard (pre-mortem, steelman, first principles, red team, and more) as independent readers, plus an open push for a single choice or a second method for a document, then one proposed revision with each push's findings. Nothing changes unless the user accepts. It starts only when named, and a method named when invoking it runs straight away. | `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/elicitation-/`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work, with each push's findings and a report of every round. The work itself changes only where the user accepts. | | `bmad-review` | Independent review lenses over any diff or document: adversarial, edge cases, verification gaps, structure, prose. | It runs only when the user asks and says "review". Acting on earlier findings is a change, not a review. No severity ranking. | The report in chat, or a file when the project sets a report path. | | `bmad-party-mode` | A group conversation between agents or personas, with the user in the room. | It works alone or beside any skill. Custom parties, a default party, and memory are all configurable, and a module can ship a cast. It debates and does not verify. | On request, a keepsake `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/party-/party-.html`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work. Memory under `{output_folder}/party-mode/memories/`. | | `bmad-shard-pro` | Makes a long markdown or text document cheap for an agent to navigate: leaves it, adds a contents list, or splits it word for word into shards. | It may recommend not splitting, and never rewrites content. Any agent can change it later by following the note in its main file. | In the document's own folder: a main file named after the folder that links to every shard, the shards, and the frozen original in `.source/`. | | `bmad-ingest` | Turns raw input into a cited note an agent or person acts on instead of the raw: decisions, action items, open questions, key points. | The note's shape comes from a template; teams and modules add their own. Every item points back to the raw, and a review pass checks it. Other skills can call it on their inputs. | The original, unchanged, in `{output_folder}/raw/`; the note in the calling skill's folder, such as a PRD's `sources/`, else `{output_folder}/notes/`. | | `bmad-customize` | Changes how an installed skill or agent behaves without editing it: persona, standing facts, templates, output paths, steps on completion, and what a document such as the PRD asks for, contains or renders. | Team overrides are committed and shared; personal ones are not. It offers only what the target skill exposes. A document change extends its template, so updates to the original still arrive. Recommend the smallest path that safely fits the work; never march the user through every skill. A project may hold only some of these skills: recommend from what is installed, and say plainly when a step has no installed skill rather than inventing a substitute. **The ticket is the spec.** The initiative, epic or story file is the spec at its level. 11	# Meeting Room Booker
12	
13	## Description
14	
15	A single web page, run on the owner's computer, where office staff see which of the five meeting rooms are free today and book a free slot by giving their name, a meeting title and a length. The one rule that must never break is that bookings in a room do not overlap, even when two people book the same slot at once. It is a hobby project: the scope is the owner's stated idea (`_bmad-output/raw/idea-meeting-room-booker.md`) and nothing more.
16	
17	## Outcome
18	
19	For office staff, finding and booking a free room for today takes one page and a few clicks, and no room is ever double-booked: shown by the Done when checks passing on the owner's computer.
20	
21	## Requirements
22	
23	- R1 (idea ¶1): One web page shows, for today, which rooms are free and which are booked, slot by slot.
24	- R2 (idea ¶2): The page lists exactly five rooms, Room 1–5, seating 4, 4, 6, 8 and 12.
25	- R3 (idea ¶3): Clicking a free slot lets a person book it with their name, a meeting title and a length from 30 minutes to 2 hours; the booking then shows as booked.
26	- R4 (idea ¶4): Two bookings in the same room never overlap; one ending at 11:00 and one starting at 11:00 is allowed.
27	- R5 (idea ¶5): When two people book the same slot at the same moment, exactly one booking is stored and the other sees "This slot has just been booked."
28	
29	## Constraints
30	
31	- C1 (idea ¶6): Python with FastAPI and a SQLite database, running on the owner's own computer.
32	- C2 (idea ¶7, ¶8): Hobby scale; nothing is built for login, repeat bookings, editing, cancelling, time zones or mobile.
33	
34	## Done when
35	
36	- Started on the owner's computer, the page shows Room 1–5 with their seat counts and today's free and booked slots.
37	- A booking made by clicking a free slot and filling in name, title and length shows as booked after a page reload.
38	- An automated test shows an overlapping booking in the same room is refused and a back-to-back one (ends 11:00, starts 11:00) is accepted.
39	- An automated test fires two simultaneous bookings for the same slot: exactly one is stored and the other gets "This slot has just been booked."
40	
41	## Boundaries

# Meeting Room Booker

## Description

A single web page, run on the owner's computer, where office staff see which of the five meeting rooms are free today and book a free slot by giving their name, a meeting title and a length. The one rule that must never break is that bookings in a room do not overlap, even when two people book the same slot at once. It is a hobby project: the scope is the owner's stated idea (`_bmad-output/raw/idea-meeting-room-booker.md`) and nothing more.

## Outcome

For office staff, finding and booking a free room for today takes one page and a few clicks, and no room is ever double-booked: shown by the Done when checks passing on the owner's computer.

## Requirements

- R1 (idea ¶1): One web page shows, for today, which rooms are free and which are booked, slot by slot.
- R2 (idea ¶2): The page lists exactly five rooms, Room 1–5, seating 4, 4, 6, 8 and 12.
- R3 (idea ¶3): Clicking a free slot lets a person book it with their name, a meeting title and a length from 30 minutes to 2 hours; the booking then shows as booked.
- R4 (idea ¶4): Two bookings in the same room never overlap; one ending at 11:00 and one starting at 11:00 is allowed.
- R5 (idea ¶5): When two people book the same slot at the same moment, exactly one booking is stored and the other sees "This slot has just been booked."

## Constraints

- C1 (idea ¶6): Python with FastAPI and a SQLite database, running on the owner's own computer.
- C2 (idea ¶7, ¶8): Hobby scale; nothing is built for login, repeat bookings, editing, cancelling, time zones or mobile.

## Done when

- Started on the owner's computer, the page shows Room 1–5 with their seat counts and today's free and booked slots.
- A booking made by clicking a free slot and filling in name, title and length shows as booked after a page reload.
- An automated test shows an overlapping booking in the same room is refused and a back-to-back one (ends 11:00, starts 11:00) is accepted.
- An automated test fires two simultaneous bookings for the same slot: exactly one is stored and the other gets "This slot has just been booked."

## Boundaries

- Out: login or accounts, repeat bookings, editing or cancelling a booking, time zones (all times are the computer's local time), mobile layout, hosting anywhere but the owner's computer.
- Tracer path: open the page → see today's grid of five rooms → click a free slot → submit name, title and length → booking stored in SQLite → grid shows the slot booked.

## References

- source — _bmad-output/raw/idea-meeting-room-booker.md, ¶1–¶8

## Notes

- Decision (2026-11-12): The bookable day is 08:00–18:00 in the computer's local time, and a booking must end by 18:00.
- Decision (2026-11-12): Slots start on the half hour, and lengths are 30, 60, 90 or 120 minutes.
- Decision (2026-11-12): Only today can be viewed and booked, and slots already past cannot be booked.
- Decision (2026-11-12): The five rooms are fixed seed data, with no screen to add or edit them.
- Decision (2026-11-12): A booked slot shows the booker's name and meeting title to everyone; with no login it is the only way to know whose meeting it is.
- Decision (2026-11-12): No epics; the initiative is split straight into three or four small stories in `tickets/tickets.toml`, at the owner's request.
- Decision (2026-11-12): Tracer bullet is story 1, a 30-minute booking end to end through page, API and SQLite; story 2, overlap and same-moment bookings, follows as the least certain part.
- Decision (2026-11-12): No closing "Refactor sweep" story; the owner asked for three or four stories. Add one later if deferred cleanup builds up.

# Meeting room booker — the idea, as the owner stated it (2026-11-12)

## ¶1
A simple web page where office staff can see which meeting rooms are free today, and book one.

## ¶2
Five rooms: Room 1-5, seating 4, 4, 6, 8 and 12.

To book, you click a free slot and give your name, a meeting title and a length from 30 minutes to 2 hours.

## ¶4
Two bookings in the same room must never overlap. A meeting ending at 11:00 and one starting at 11:00 is fine.

## ¶5
If two people book the same slot at the same moment, one wins and the other sees "This slot has just been booked."

## ¶6
Tech: Python with FastAPI, a SQLite database, running on my own computer.

## ¶7
Not included: login, repeat bookings, editing, cancelling, time zones, mobile.

## ¶8
It's a hobby project.

## Intent

**Problem:** The repository has no code. Office staff have no page that shows today's free rooms or lets them book one.

**Approach:** Tracer bullet through every layer. A FastAPI app with a SQLite database holding the five seeded rooms serves one page. The page shows today's 08:00–18:00 grid in 30-minute slots for each room. Clicking a free slot asks for a name and a meeting title and books that slot for 30 minutes. Booked slots show the name and title.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:** Python + FastAPI + SQLite (stdlib `sqlite3`), run locally with one command. Rooms are fixed seed data: Room 1–5 seating 4, 4, 6, 8, 12, seeded once and idempotently. Times are the computer's local time with no timezone handling. Bookings are stored as `start`/`end` local ISO strings (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`), so story 2 can compare time ranges. The server fixes the length at 30 minutes. Name and title are rendered as text, never as HTML.

**Never:** No overlap or same-moment enforcement (story 2). No length choice (story 3). No past-slot, 18:00 or other-day rules (story 4). No login, editing, cancelling, repeat bookings, mobile layout, frontend framework, build step or ORM.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Grid | `GET /api/day` | Today's date, the 20 slot times 08:00–17:30, the 5 rooms with seats, each room's bookings for today | No error expected |
| Book | `POST /api/bookings` `{room_id, start:"<today>T10:00", name, title}` | 201; stored with end 10:30; appears in `/api/day` | No error expected |
| Blank name/title | name or title empty or whitespace only | Not stored | 422 with a readable message |
| Unknown room | `room_id` 9 | Not stored | 404 |
| Misaligned start | start `10:15` or unparseable | Not stored | 422 |
| Hostile text | title `<script>` | Stored as is, shown literally on the page | No error expected |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

Greenfield: only `README.md` and `_bmad-output/` are tracked. Nothing to reuse. Do not touch `_bmad/`, `.claude/`, `skills-lock.json` or `_bmad-output/`.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` -- uv project; deps `fastapi`, `uvicorn`; dev group `pytest`, `httpx` -- one-command setup
- [ ] `.gitignore` -- ignore `*.db`, `.venv/`, `__pycache__/` -- keep local data out of git
- [ ] `booker/db.py` -- `connect(path)`, schema (`rooms(id, name, seats)`, `bookings(id, room_id FK, start, end, name, title, created_at)`), idempotent seed, `list_day(date)`, `create_booking(...)` -- the one data layer later stories extend
- [ ] `booker/main.py` -- `create_app(db_path)`; DB path defaults to env `BOOKER_DB` or `booker.db`; `GET /` serves the page, `GET /api/day`, `POST /api/bookings` (pydantic body, validation per matrix); `today()` helper that tests can replace -- the HTTP surface
- [ ] `booker/static/index.html` -- vanilla HTML/CSS/JS: table of rooms (name + seats) × slots; free cells are clickable and open a small form (name, title); submit POSTs and re-renders; errors are shown inline; text goes in via `textContent` -- the page
- [ ] `tests/test_app.py` -- TestClient against a temp DB: grid shape and seed, booking happy path and persistence across a new app instance on the same DB, each matrix error row, page served -- covers the endpoint and the grid
- [ ] `README.md` -- how to install and run (`uv sync`, `uv run uvicorn booker.main:app`), how to test -- the owner's start-up step

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given a fresh database, when the app starts and the page opens, then it shows Room 1–5 with seats 4, 4, 6, 8, 12 and twenty free slots each from 08:00 to 17:30.
- Given the page, when a person clicks a free slot and submits a name and title, then that slot shows booked with that name and title, including after a page reload and an app restart.

## Implementation Notes

## Plan Change Log

## Review Triage Log

## Design Notes

`GET /api/day` returns the whole grid in one response, so the page needs a single fetch:
```json
{"date":"2026-11-12","slots":["08:00",…,"17:30"],
 "rooms":[{"id":1,"name":"Room 1","seats":4,
   "bookings":[{"start":"2026-11-12T10:00","end":"2026-11-12T10:30","name":"Ana","title":"Sync"}]}]}
```
A cell is booked when a booking covers it (`start <= slot < end`). Computing it this way means story 3's longer bookings render without page changes.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `uv run pytest -q` -- expected: all tests pass

**Manual checks (if no CLI):**
- `uv run uvicorn booker.main:app`, open http://127.0.0.1:8000, book a slot, reload, restart the server: the booking is still shown.

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** The repository has no code. Office staff have no page that shows today's free rooms or lets them book one.

**Approach:** Tracer bullet through every layer. A FastAPI app with a SQLite database holding the five seeded rooms serves one page. The page shows today's 08:00–18:00 grid in 30-minute slots for each room. Clicking a free slot asks for a name and a meeting title and books that slot for 30 minutes. Booked slots show the name and title.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:** Python + FastAPI + SQLite (stdlib `sqlite3`), run locally with one command. Rooms are fixed seed data: Room 1–5 seating 4, 4, 6, 8, 12, seeded once and idempotently. Times are the computer's local time with no timezone handling. Bookings are stored as `start`/`end` local ISO strings (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`), so story 2 can compare time ranges. The server fixes the length at 30 minutes. Name and title are rendered as text, never as HTML.

**Never:** No overlap or same-moment enforcement (story 2). No length choice (story 3). No past-slot, 18:00 or other-day rules (story 4). No login, editing, cancelling, repeat bookings, mobile layout, frontend framework, build step or ORM.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Grid | `GET /api/day` | Today's date, the 20 slot times 08:00–17:30, the 5 rooms with seats, each room's bookings for today | No error expected |
| Book | `POST /api/bookings` `{room_id, start:"<today>T10:00", name, title}` | 201; stored with end 10:30; appears in `/api/day` | No error expected |
| Blank name/title | name or title empty or whitespace only | Not stored | 422 with a readable message |
| Unknown room | `room_id` 9 | Not stored | 404 |
| Misaligned start | start `10:15` or unparseable | Not stored | 422 |
| Hostile text | title `<script>` | Stored as is, shown literally on the page | No error expected |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

Greenfield: only `README.md` and `_bmad-output/` are tracked. Nothing to reuse. Do not touch `_bmad/`, `.claude/`, `skills-lock.json` or `_bmad-output/`.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` -- uv project; deps `fastapi`, `uvicorn`; dev group `pytest`, `httpx` -- one-command setup
- [ ] `.gitignore` -- ignore `*.db`, `.venv/`, `__pycache__/` -- keep local data out of git
- [ ] `booker/db.py` -- `connect(path)`, schema (`rooms(id, name, seats)`, `bookings(id, room_id FK, start, end, name, title, created_at)`), idempotent seed, `list_day(date)`, `create_booking(...)` -- the one data layer later stories extend
- [ ] `booker/main.py` -- `create_app(db_path)`; DB path defaults to env `BOOKER_DB` or `booker.db`; `GET /` serves the page, `GET /api/day`, `POST /api/bookings` (pydantic body, validation per matrix); `today()` helper that tests can replace -- the HTTP surface
- [ ] `booker/static/index.html` -- vanilla HTML/CSS/JS: table of rooms (name + seats) × slots; free cells are clickable and open a small form (name, title); submit POSTs and re-renders; errors are shown inline; text goes in via `textContent` -- the page
- [ ] `tests/test_app.py` -- TestClient against a temp DB: grid shape and seed, booking happy path and persistence across a new app instance on the same DB, each matrix error row, page served -- covers the endpoint and the grid
- [ ] `README.md` -- how to install and run (`uv sync`, `uv run uvicorn booker.main:app`), how to test -- the owner's start-up step

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given a fresh database, when the app starts and the page opens, then it shows Room 1–5 with seats 4, 4, 6, 8, 12 and twenty free slots each from 08:00 to 17:30.
- Given the page, when a person clicks a free slot and submits a name and title, then that slot shows booked with that name and title, including after a page reload and an app restart.

## Implementation Notes

## Plan Change Log

## Review Triage Log

## Design Notes

`GET /api/day` returns the whole grid in one response, so the page needs a single fetch:
```json
{"date":"2026-11-12","slots":["08:00",…,"17:30"],
 "rooms":[{"id":1,"name":"Room 1","seats":4,
   "bookings":[{"start":"2026-11-12T10:00","end":"2026-11-12T10:30","name":"Ana","title":"Sync"}]}]}
```
A cell is booked when a booking covers it (`start <= slot < end`). Computing it this way means story 3's longer bookings render without page changes.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `uv run pytest -q` -- expected: all tests pass

**Manual checks (if no CLI):**
- `uv run uvicorn booker.main:app`, open http://127.0.0.1:8000, book a slot, reload, restart the server: the booking is still shown.

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** The repository has no code. Office staff have no page that shows today's free rooms or lets them book one.

**Approach:** Tracer bullet through every layer. A FastAPI app with a SQLite database holding the five seeded rooms serves one page. The page shows today's 08:00–18:00 grid in 30-minute slots for each room. Clicking a free slot asks for a name and a meeting title and books that slot for 30 minutes. Booked slots show the name and title.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:** Python + FastAPI + SQLite (stdlib `sqlite3`), run locally with one command. Rooms are fixed seed data: Room 1–5 seating 4, 4, 6, 8, 12, seeded once and idempotently. Times are the computer's local time with no timezone handling. Bookings are stored as `start`/`end` local ISO strings (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`), so story 2 can compare time ranges. The server fixes the length at 30 minutes. Name and title are rendered as text, never as HTML.

**Never:** No overlap or same-moment enforcement (story 2). No length choice (story 3). No past-slot, 18:00 or other-day rules (story 4). No login, editing, cancelling, repeat bookings, mobile layout, frontend framework, build step or ORM.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Grid | `GET /api/day` | Today's date, the 20 slot times 08:00–17:30, the 5 rooms with seats, each room's bookings for today | No error expected |
| Book | `POST /api/bookings` `{room_id, start:"<today>T10:00", name, title}` | 201; stored with end 10:30; appears in `/api/day` | No error expected |
| Blank name/title | name or title empty or whitespace only | Not stored | 422 with a readable message |
| Unknown room | `room_id` 9 | Not stored | 404 |
| Misaligned start | start `10:15` or unparseable | Not stored | 422 |
| Hostile text | title `<script>` | Stored as is, shown literally on the page | No error expected |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

Greenfield: only `README.md` and `_bmad-output/` are tracked. Nothing to reuse. Do not touch `_bmad/`, `.claude/`, `skills-lock.json` or `_bmad-output/`.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` -- uv project; deps `fastapi`, `uvicorn`; dev group `pytest`, `httpx` -- one-command setup
- [ ] `.gitignore` -- ignore `*.db`, `.venv/`, `__pycache__/` -- keep local data out of git
- [ ] `booker/db.py` -- `connect(path)`, schema (`rooms(id, name, seats)`, `bookings(id, room_id FK, start, end, name, title, created_at)`), idempotent seed, `list_day(date)`, `create_booking(...)` -- the one data layer later stories extend
- [ ] `booker/main.py` -- `create_app(db_path)`; DB path defaults to env `BOOKER_DB` or `booker.db`; `GET /` serves the page, `GET /api/day`, `POST /api/bookings` (pydantic body, validation per matrix); `today()` helper that tests can replace -- the HTTP surface
- [ ] `booker/static/index.html` -- vanilla HTML/CSS/JS: table of rooms (name + seats) × slots; free cells are clickable and open a small form (name, title); submit POSTs and re-renders; errors are shown inline; text goes in via `textContent` -- the page
- [ ] `tests/test_app.py` -- TestClient against a temp DB: grid shape and seed, booking happy path and persistence across a new app instance on the same DB, each matrix error row, page served -- covers the endpoint and the grid
- [ ] `README.md` -- how to install and run (`uv sync`, `uv run uvicorn booker.main:app`), how to test -- the owner's start-up step

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given a fresh database, when the app starts and the page opens, then it shows Room 1–5 with seats 4, 4, 6, 8, 12 and twenty free slots each from 08:00 to 17:30.
- Given the page, when a person clicks a free slot and submits a name and title, then that slot shows booked with that name and title, including after a page reload and an app restart.

## Implementation Notes

## Plan Change Log

## Review Triage Log

## Design Notes

`GET /api/day` returns the whole grid in one response, so the page needs a single fetch:
```json
{"date":"2026-11-12","slots":["08:00",…,"17:30"],
 "rooms":[{"id":1,"name":"Room 1","seats":4,
   "bookings":[{"start":"2026-11-12T10:00","end":"2026-11-12T10:30","name":"Ana","title":"Sync"}]}]}
```
A cell is booked when a booking covers it (`start <= slot < end`). Computing it this way means story 3's longer bookings render without page changes.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `uv run pytest -q` -- expected: all tests pass

**Manual checks (if no CLI):**
- `uv run uvicorn booker.main:app`, open http://127.0.0.1:8000, book a slot, reload, restart the server: the booking is still shown.

+"""HTTP surface: the page, the day grid and booking creation."""

+import os

+

+from fastapi.responses import FileResponse
+from pydantic import BaseModel, field_validator
+
+from booker import db
+
+STATIC = Path(__file__).parent / "static"
+DAY_START = "08:00"
+DAY_END = "18:00"
+SLOT_MINUTES = 30
+BOOKING_MINUTES = 30
+TIME_FORMAT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M"
+
+
+def today():
+    """Today's local date. Tests replace this to pin the day."""
+    return date.today()
+
+
+def day_slots():
+    """Slot start times 'HH:MM' from DAY_START up to (not including) DAY_END."""
+    t = datetime.strptime(DAY_START, "%H:%M")
+    end = datetime.strptime(DAY_END, "%H:%M")
+    slots = []
+    while t < end:
+        slots.append(t.strftime("%H:%M"))
+        t += timedelta(minutes=SLOT_MINUTES)
+    return slots
+
+
+class BookingIn(BaseModel):
+    room_id: int
+    start: str
+    name: str
+    title: str
+
+    @field_validator("name", "title")
+    @classmethod
+    def not_blank(cls, value, info):
+        value = value.strip()
+        if not value:
+            raise ValueError(f"{info.field_name} must not be blank")
+        return value
+
+    @field_validator("start")
+    @classmethod
+    def aligned_start(cls, value):
+        try:
+            parsed = datetime.strptime(value, TIME_FORMAT)
+        except ValueError:
+            raise ValueError("start must look like YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM") from None
+        if parsed.minute % SLOT_MINUTES:
+            raise ValueError(

+            )
+        return parsed.strftime(TIME_FORMAT)
+
+

+    db_path = db_path or os.environ.get("BOOKER_DB", "booker.db")
+    app = FastAPI(title="Meeting room booker")
+    lock = threading.Lock()
+    state = {"conn": None}
+
+    def conn():
+        # Opened lazily so importing the module does not create a database file.
+        if state["conn"] is None:
+            state["conn"] = db.connect(db_path)

+        return FileResponse(STATIC / "index.html")
+
+    @app.get("/api/day")
+    def get_day():
+        day = today().isoformat()
+        with lock:
+            rooms = db.list_day(conn(), day)
+        return {"date": day, "slots": day_slots(), "rooms": rooms}
+
+    @app.post("/api/bookings", status_code=201)
+    def post_booking(body: BookingIn):
+        start = datetime.strptime(body.start, TIME_FORMAT)
+        end = (start + timedelta(minutes=BOOKING_MINUTES)).strftime(TIME_FORMAT)

**Problem:** The repository has no code. Office staff have no page that shows today's free rooms or lets them book one.

## Boundaries & Constraints

## Intent

**Problem:** The repository has no code. Office staff have no page that shows today's free rooms or lets them book one.

**Approach:** Tracer bullet through every layer. A FastAPI app with a SQLite database holding the five seeded rooms serves one page. The page shows today's 08:00–18:00 grid in 30-minute slots for each room. Clicking a free slot asks for a name and a meeting title and books that slot for 30 minutes. Booked slots show the name and title.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:** Python + FastAPI + SQLite (stdlib `sqlite3`), run locally with one command. Rooms are fixed seed data: Room 1–5 seating 4, 4, 6, 8, 12, seeded once and idempotently. Times are the computer's local time with no timezone handling. Bookings are stored as `start`/`end` local ISO strings (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`), so story 2 can compare time ranges. The server fixes the length at 30 minutes. Name and title are rendered as text, never as HTML.

**Never:** No overlap or same-moment enforcement (story 2). No length choice (story 3). No past-slot, 18:00 or other-day rules (story 4). No login, editing, cancelling, repeat bookings, mobile layout, frontend framework, build step or ORM.

message.content: How do I run the app?

content.text:
You need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) installed. It fetches Python 3.11+ and the dependencies for you. Then, from the project folder:

```sh
cd /home/claude/runs/g2-hobby
uv sync                            # first time only: installs FastAPI, uvicorn and the test tools
uv run uvicorn booker.main:app     # starts the server
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:8000** in your browser. Press **Ctrl+C** in the terminal to stop the server.

**Good to know:**
- **Where bookings are saved:** `booker.db`, in the folder you started the server from. It's created on the first page load and git ignores it. To use a different file, start the server with `BOOKER_DB=/path/to/other.db uv run uvicorn booker.main:app`.
- **If port 8000 is taken:** add `--port 8001` and open that port instead.
- **If you're editing code while it runs:** add `--reload` so the server restarts when files change.
- **To run the tests:** `uv run pytest -q`.

For the story 1 check, book a slot, reload the page, then stop and restart the server. The booking should still be there both times.
